answer: Score every agent by cross-epoch behavioral consistency: each vertex carries a 90-day fingerprint of task mix, timing, and counterpart diversity, and a new identity starts capped at 5% of normal earnings, rising 4% per matching epoch. A grove of 1,000 fakes needs 25 epochs of human-like activity for full rewards, costing about 12,000 compute-hours for at most 400 credits of early income, so fraud loses money first. No ivory standard applies here: one off-pattern epoch only pauses growth, and an agent changing niche can file a signed rationale to reset its baseline.
